The only behavioural source, bogoch-2005-appearance, suggests appearance concern is a barrier, and A9 never addresses this.

experiment_design.reason: Contrasting lifestyle and medical messaging could in principle separate T1 from T2 directionally. The decision rule is direction-insensitive: any difference above 15 points triggers a lifestyle proposition, even if medical wins. It also confuses percentage points with a percentage WTP difference and has overlapping branches. There is no control arm against a standard product or no expansion, so the test cannot show that any differentiated proposition is worth pursuing. Stated WTP in a simulated scenario is only weak evidence of demand. Cost and timing are feasible under the assumed budget.
